claims.claim: A risk register is a repository in which outputs of risk-management processes are recorded; a current GAO report describes it as a tool that describes and tracks risks and records specific mitigation strategies.

Useful risk-register information can include the person responsible for managing a risk, probability, impact, a score where a context uses one, planned responses, and other information needed to understand individual risks; the exact fields are context-dependent.

PMI defines a risk owner as the person responsible for monitoring a risk and selecting and implementing an appropriate response strategy; assigning a named owner makes responsibility visible but does not by itself transfer organizational authority.
A register should be updated as risks and risk actions change; an entry's status helps readers distinguish active, changed, or closed records but is not evidence that uncertainty has disappeared.

A risk management plan explains how risk-management activities will be accomplished, a risk register records and tracks individual risks, and a risk report summarizes risk information for communication; these artifacts have related but different jobs.
A cause-event-effect statement makes a risk entry more reviewable than a label alone because it connects a plausible condition, uncertain event, and possible effect on an objective.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Sources show different field sets and operating detail for risk registers.
positions: The PMI lexicon gives a concise definition of the register and risk-owner role.
GAO lists example fields and relates the register to a plan and report in a large public program.
PMI practice articles describe additional fields and project-specific practices.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson treats a register as a maintained, context-dependent repository. It teaches a small set of commonly useful fields without declaring any one template, score, status vocabulary, cadence, or authority model mandatory.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft supplied only generic placeholder prose, an incomplete Eli-10 block, and three three-option quick-check items. It did not define a risk register, explain fields or ownership, distinguish related artifacts, or cite evidence.
correctionsNeeded: Replaced boilerplate with original, source-grounded instruction about the register as a maintained information artifact.
Added a bounded, hypothetical student-exhibit entry to show how description, assessment, ownership, response, status, and review relate.
Separated risk-register documentation from the broader risk-management process and from risk reporting; excluded enterprise-specific and prescriptive advice.
Replaced the generated three-option questions with five independently checked four-option items.
rightsIssues: GAO-25-108466 is a U.S. government publication used as a public-domain factual source; no source prose, tables, or figures are reproduced.
PMI materials are treated as reference-only. Terminology and distinctions were checked live, but all lesson prose, examples, and question wording are original.

questionKeyCheck.method: Read every saved prompt, option set, correctIndex, explanation, and sourceIds after writing.
questionKeyCheck.result: Exactly five four-option questions cover recall, understanding, application, and analysis. C and D both occur; all A/B/C/D positions occur, and no position appears more than twice.

sourceRecords.title: ICBM Modernization: Air Force Actions Needed to Expeditiously Address Critical Risks to Sentinel Transition (GAO-25-108466)
sourceRecords.notes: Checked live through GAO's accessible PDF. Pages 11–13 distinguish the risk management plan, register, and report; explain that a register describes and tracks risks and records mitigation strategies; and list example information including responsibility, probability, impact, score, and planned responses. Used only for transferable introductory concepts, not its defense-program recommendations.

sourceRecords.title: PMI Lexicon of Project Management Terms, Version 5.0
sourceRecords.notes: Official PMI lexicon was checked live through search results after the direct PDF returned a 403. It supports the definitions of risk register, risk management plan, risk owner, and risk response. No source prose, diagrams, or templates were adapted.

sourceRecords.title: The Meaning of Risk in an Uncertain World
sourceRecords.notes: Checked live. Supports using a risk description that connects cause, event, and effect, and gives examples of information that may be included as appropriate. The lesson does not treat the article's field list or links to project plans as a universal template.

sourceRecords.title: Risk Management - Beyond the Textbooks
sourceRecords.notes: Checked live. Supports the general point that a register or database should reflect current risk and risk-action status rather than remain static. It is used only to support the lesson's review and status discussion.
